Explore the full course and mastery checkpoints

Learn it. Build it. Explain it.

For each lesson: read the explanation, trace the example by hand, solve both problems, then explain correctness and complexity without notes. Revisit a fresh variation after 2 days and again after a week.

Progress is evidence, not a promise: completing lessons or passing the supplied tests does not guarantee professional proficiency or a hiring outcome. Use unfamiliar problems and repeated independent performance to assess readiness.

Your checkpoint rubric

Score yourself 0–3 on each skill: understanding requirements, choosing and justifying an algorithm, writing readable code, complexity analysis, edge-case testing, and explaining your reasoning. 0 = missing; 1 = major help; 2 = mostly independent; 3 = independent and well explained.

Move on when you consistently reach at least 2 in every skill across new problems on different days and can re-solve a delayed variation without notes. This is a course guideline, not a company hiring cutoff.

Interview focus

Microsoft: clarify requirements, plan, write real code, test boundaries, and discuss time/space tradeoffs. Meta-oriented practice: communicate clearly, recognize patterns, justify your approach, and verify code by hand. Timers here are practice targets, not promised company interview formats.

For experienced SWE roles, coding is only part of preparation. Separately practice role-appropriate system design and truthful behavioral stories about collaboration, learning, impact, conflict and feedback. Confirm your actual interview format, language and tool rules with the recruiter.

Sources: Microsoft technical guidance · Microsoft interview tips · Meta-authored guide (third-party mirror; current applicability unverified). Reviewed October 2, 2026.
